chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Shu'ayb Abu Salih, from Khalid Abu Al-A'la Al-Khaffaf, who said:
I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and upon him was a green gown (burd), and he was in Ihram.

key_terms.أَخْضَرُ: Green, describing the color of the garment.
key_terms.بُرْدٌ: A type of outer garment or cloak, often rectangular and sewn or folded, worn over the Ihram clothes.
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One who is in the state of Ihram, a sacred state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah.

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam wear while in Ihram according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* provides a crucial narrative precedent for the permissibility of wearing sewn garments, specifically a green *burd* (outer cloak), during Ihram, challenging the stricter view that only unsewn white cloths are allowed. In Shia jurisprudence, this observation by Khalid al-Khaffaf is often cited to support the view that the prohibition applies primarily to the specific undergarments, while outer layers like the *burd* remain permissible, reflecting the practical flexibility of the Imams' conduct. The green color also holds symbolic significance in Shia tradition, often associated with the Prophet's family and paradise.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Shuayb Abu Salih, from Khalid Abu Al A’ala Al Khaffaf who said,
‘I saw Abu Ja’farasws and upon himasws was a green gown, and heasws was in Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Shu’ayb abu Salih from Khalid abu al-‘Ala’ al-Khaffaf who has said the following: “
I saw abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in the state of Ihram with a green gown on him.”
